title: Snowstorm drive to New York for Melrose recordings
summary: Burton drives through a night snowstorm over the mountains to make a four-day recording engagement, but strains his voice and cannot sing his solos.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Roy Palmer. P-A-L-M-E-R. The reason why this sticks out about talking about Roy Palmer, an awful experience, a sad experience, but a great experience. We went to New York to make a bunch of records under Melrose Management Center.
We had two cars. Well, Roy told me about it. You went with him once over there.

Well, and I did the driving because when we get to Philadelphia and come out of Philadelphia going to New York, we run into one of them electric snow storms. And up in the Alligator Mountains, there was no good road then. And Melrose was nervous because this recording engagement was set at this particular morning at that certain time, at that date, and he had four days engaged. And if you don't make it on time, we lose the whole four days. And so I strained myself by taking the wheel, and I says, I've had so much driving experience, I drove mostly all my life, fortunately. And so, and still driving. I said, listen, I'll tell you what we'll do. I said, we can't stop on this road. If we stop, I says, the way this snowstorm is, somebody's allowed to run into us and push us off the mountain. And I says, I'll drive at 10 miles an hour, and somebody keep wiping the windshield as much as they can. And by the time of daybreak, we'll be so near in New York, see, then we can pick up speed and get in there and make this recording engagement. Now here's where the sad part for me to come. Going through all that strain, making all that driving, all that night at 10 miles an hour, and then when daybreak come, and it did kind of let up a little bit, and then speed it up as much as it could to get into New York City. When I get into New York City, don't have time to do nothing but just take a bath and freshen up, well, that strain told on my throat. Couldn't sing. And I get down there, and I've got an, I don't know how many numbers at that time, set the record by myself that was going to help me on this recording engagement outside the Mother Normandy recording that was going to do with the band, and we had two or three different outfits with us. And that's when I started killing myself.
I was thinking you were going to say you had a wreck, but it could have been worse if you had a wreck on there.
